statement: The distance $d(t)$, in meters, that a stone has fallen $t$ seconds after it is dropped from a tall bridge is modeled by $d(t) = 4.9t^2$. According to the model, what is the value of $d(3) - d(2)$?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the inputs first and computed $d(3 - 2) = d(1)$.
I found $d(3) = 44.1$ and then subtracted the number $2$ instead of subtracting $d(2)$.
I doubled $t$ instead of squaring it, so I computed $4.9(6) - 4.9(4)$.

solutions.reliable: $d(3) = 4.9(3)^2 = 44.1$ and $d(2) = 4.9(2)^2 = 19.6$, so $d(3) - d(2) = 44.1 - 19.6 = 24.5$ meters. This is how far the stone falls during the third second.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
